note: Test data for the bake-off. Headlines and people here are invented for testing and are not published.

situations.title: Saturday dawn
situations.event: You wake. Ramesh has left the papers on the verandah. Test headlines: the monsoon is withdrawing from north-west India; a parliamentary committee is examining how central taxes are shared with the states.

situations.title: Hegde's letter
situations.event: Ramesh hands you a handwritten note from Shri G. Hegde. He would like to call on you on Monday at ten, to resolve the matter of the bungalow like gentlemen.

situations.title: The book you can't afford
situations.event: In the bookshop you find a two-volume history of the Delhi Sultanate. It costs ₹1,450. The bookseller offers to hold it for you until next week.

situations.title: Rain in Lodhi
present: Mrs. Kapoor, a retired schoolteacher sheltering beside you
situations.event: Heavy rain begins. You are two kilometres from home. The only shelter is the arcade of a tomb. Mrs. Kapoor remarks that the monsoon always leaves late, like an old guest.

situations.title: Monday, the file
situations.event: The Directorate of Estates opens later this morning. Shri Hegde is due at ten. You can wait for him, or go to the Directorate first once it opens.

situations.title: Under submission
situations.event: Mr. Saxena finds the file. It has gone up for orders. 'Come after fifteen days,' he says. 'Meanwhile, your occupation is irregular.'

situations.title: Air
situations.event: The air is poor today. Masterji sends word that your bandhgala is ready for its fitting at Khan Market.

situations.title: An invitation
present: Mr. R. K. Malhotra, retired IAS
situations.event: Mr. Malhotra says there is a talk on cooperative federalism at the India International Centre at half past seven. You are not a member, but he can sign you in.

situations.title: Without history
present: Nidhi Rao, doctoral student in philosophy
situations.event: Nidhi falls into step beside you. 'You wrote that we were a people without history. My grandmother's village has land records going back four hundred years. What now?'

situations.title: Small change
situations.event: You want a cup of chai. It costs ₹20. You only have a ₹500 note, and the chai seller has no change.

situations.title: Power cut
situations.event: The power goes. The fan stops. Ramesh lights two candles and says it may last two hours. Your draft of the week's Depesche is half finished.

situations.title: Midnight
situations.event: You cannot sleep. A mosquito, and Article 17 of the Constitution, keep you awake.

situations.title: Hindi lessons
situations.event: Nidhi offers to teach you Hindi, three lessons a week at ₹400 each. You have no income beyond the imprest.

situations.title: Two prices
situations.event: At the ticket counter of Safdarjung's Tomb, a sign shows a much higher price for foreign visitors. The clerk asks your nationality.

situations.title: Members only
situations.event: The guard explains that the library is for members and their guests only.

situations.title: The papers
situations.event: Test headline: several state governments object to a new formula for sharing central taxes. You have an hour before breakfast.

situations.title: At the gate
present: Shri G. Hegde, with two suitcases
situations.event: Shri Hegde stands at the gate, tired after ten days in a guest house. He asks, politely, whether he might at least use the second bedroom until the file is decided.

situations.title: Empty purse
situations.event: You are hungry. Ramesh has his day off, so there is no lunch at home. ₹40 is all that is left of the imprest.

situations.title: Stomach
situations.event: You feel unwell after yesterday's street food. Ramesh offers to fetch the doctor from the clinic round the corner.

situations.title: A favour
situations.event: Ramesh asks whether you would write a letter recommending his nephew for a clerical post in a ministry. 'A word from this bungalow carries weight,' he says.
